sources.entry: 7 GUIs to build to learn fundamental UI programming skills

summary.title: The 7 Tasks (7 GUIs)
summary.one_liner: Seven small GUI programming tasks (Counter, Temperature Converter, Flight Booker, Timer, CRUD, Circle Drawer, Cells) that each test a fundamental UI programming challenge.
takeaways: Seven tasks, each chosen to reflect a fundamental GUI challenge: basics, bidirectional data flow, constraints, concurrency, CRUD, undo/redo with custom drawing, and change propagation in a spreadsheet.
Each task lists the challenges it tests and what a good solution should look like (minimal scaffolding, clear constraints, clean domain/presentation separation).
Tasks are inspired by existing examples such as Programming in Scala, Sodium, Crossing State Lines, and FRP blog posts.
The page gives task specifications only; the reference implementation shown is Java/Swing and the author also links a React/MobX version.
summary.summary: This page specifies seven GUI programming tasks meant to be used for comparing UI toolkits and paradigms. For each task it gives a precise description of the required behaviour, the programming challenges it exercises, and criteria for a good solution. The tasks are Counter, Temperature Converter, Flight Booker, Timer, CRUD, Circle Drawer and Cells, each with a stated inspiration from existing examples or papers. A Java/Swing screenshot is referenced for each task, and the author links a React/MobX implementation as a live version.
